Install HYB26-skill on Windows

1. Install Python 3.10 or newer. In PowerShell, check:
       python --version
   If this opens the Microsoft Store or Python is missing, install Python
   before continuing.

2. Keep the complete Windows package together. Open PowerShell in that folder:
       .\install-skill.ps1
   If Windows blocks this trusted local installer:
       powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\install-skill.ps1"
   This override applies only to that process. Do not change machine policy.

3. The package is copied to:
       $HOME\.copilot\skills\hyb26-skill
   Check:
       copilot skill list
   In an open CLI session, use /skills reload or restart the session.
   Rerun the installer from the updated package when you want to update it.
   Existing unrelated files are not deleted.

4. Open a separate badge project folder before asking Copilot to build an app.
   Do not use the skill installation folder as the project. Git is optional.
   Use the PowerShell commands in SKILL.md. Replace E:\ with the actual
   BADGER drive letter. Eject BADGER in File Explorer before pressing RESET.
   RP2350 is a firmware drive, not the destination for apps.

REPOSITORY-LOCAL INSTALL

Instead of a personal install, copy the complete package into:
       <your-project>\.github\skills\hyb26-skill
Set the scripts path as shown in SKILL.md. Do not install both platform
packages under different names in the same client; they are the same skill.

CHECK THE RESULT

In Copilot CLI, ask:
       Use hyb26-skill to explain how to validate a badge app and whether I
       can change its badge menu icon. Do not change any files.

The answer must use the bundled validation tool, explain that file checks
do not prove hardware behavior, and state that current event firmware does
not support custom app menu icons. icon.png is a preview image only.

For VS Code or another Copilot client, first verify its supported skill
locations in its official documentation. Restart/reload the client and run
the same prompt. Do not assume CLI discovery proves discovery in that client.
This package does not change client settings, models, or account policies.
